title: Vibeprint: how does an iPad sketch survive a page reload?
scope: Direct LAN canvas sync only: iPad browser, local vibeprint daemon, and .vibeprint/canvas.json on disk.
omissions: MCP agent tools, AI map redraws and the Fly relay path
Marks/chat persistence, image assets and git checkpoints

nodes.label: iPad browser
nodes.description: Canvas editor; keeps unacked ops in memory

nodes.label: Daemon
nodes.description: Token-gated LAN server; owns live canvas

nodes.label: canvas.json
nodes.description: Canvas shapes on disk in the repo

notes.title: Loss window
notes.text: The daemon acks an op once it is applied in memory. The save runs on an 800ms timer after the last edit, so a daemon crash before the timer fires loses the latest edits.

notes.title: Reload vs reconnect
notes.text: If the socket drops, the browser retries with backoff (500ms up to 10s). On the new snapshot it replays its unacked ops, but those live only in page memory, so a full reload drops them.

notes.title: Corrupt file stops loading
notes.text: If canvas.json won't parse or isn't a Vibeprint canvas, loading throws and says to restore it from git. A single unreadable shape is skipped and logged.
